source.filename: 2017_wang-SMA based Soft Gripper with VS for compliant and Effective Gasping .pdf

constitutive_assumptions: Composite hinge bending rigidity can be modeled as the sum of PDMS matrix and SMP structure flexural rigidities based on linear elastic beam theory
Negligible volume and structural contribution of embedded SMA wires to hinge flexural modulus
Shape memory polymer exhibits two distinct discrete elastic modulus states: glassy state (2.15 GPa) below Tg and rubbery state (10 MPa) above Tg
One-dimensional thermomechanical constitutive behavior (Brinson model) assumed for SMA bending deformation
Coulomb friction condition and quasi-static 2D vertical force equilibrium assumed during object grasping
control_variables: Finger dimensions (120 mm length, 20 mm width, 3 mm thickness)
Hinge length (15 mm) and spacing between hinges (20 mm)
SMA wire diameter (0.15 mm) and offset distance from neutral axis (1 mm)
SMP structure dimensions (15 mm length, 5 mm width, 1.5 mm thickness)
PDMS matrix mixing ratio (10:1 base-to-catalyst) and curing condition (8 hours at 55 °C)
Fixed cylinder diameter in pulling test (80 mm)
Support span (48 mm) and span-to-depth ratio (16:1) in three-point bending tests
dependent_variables: SMP and SMA temperatures during heating and cooling cycles
Bending elastic modulus of the composite hinge in glassy and rubbery states
Finger bending posture and deformation configuration
Vertical pulling / grasping force of the gripper
Static and dynamic coefficients of friction between contact materials and 3D-printed ABS
Grasping success and stability across different object geometries and masses

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Embedding 3D-printed shape memory polymer (SMP) structures inside soft composite hinges enables an approximate 55-fold reversible change in bending modulus between glassy and rubbery states (128.48 MPa vs. 2.31 MPa).

Actuation of symmetrically placed off-center SMA wires combined with selective heating of two independent SMP hinges enables a single soft robotic finger to achieve nine distinct active configurations and retain them with high stiffness.
Modulating hinge stiffness from low to high after conforming to an object increases the soft gripper's maximum vertical pulling force by approximately 10 times (from 0.6 N to 5.8 N).

The bending modulus of the composite variable-stiffness hinge can be theoretically predicted using second moment of area formulations and constituent elastic moduli, showing agreement within 5.6% and 1.7% of experimental values.

Integrating a soft Ecoflex layer at the fingertip pad increases compliant contact area and moment resistance, preventing slippage and allowing stable grasping of difficult frustum-shaped geometries compared to rigid point contacts.

Heating the SMP to rubbery state requires approximately 35 seconds, whereas passive cooling back to the glassy state requires approximately 240 seconds, representing the primary operational time bottleneck.

experimental_setup: Thermal imaging setup using a CX-320U thermal camera at 27 °C ambient temperature to monitor real-time heating and cooling of SMP and SMA
Ni-Cr wire heating circuit supplying 0.3 A (0.98 W per SMP structure) for thermal phase transition of SMP
Joule heating circuit supplying 0.65 A (2.79 W) to SMA wires for active bending actuation
Universal testing machine (Instron 5948 MicroTester) equipped with a three-point flexure fixture (2810-400) for ASTM D 790-03 bending modulus testing
Universal testing machine with friction fixture (2810-005) for ASTM D 1894 coefficient of friction evaluation of PDMS and Ecoflex on 3D-printed ABS
Upward vertical pulling test setup measuring retention force on an 80 mm diameter fixed cylinder across a 32.5 mm vertical displacement

Physical grasp testing on diverse real-world objects: a lightweight deformable cylinder (2.1 g), a fragile uncooked egg (51.9 g), an irregular heavy red pepper (143.2 g), and a 3D-printed ABS frustum-shaped object
Continuous 100-cycle (approx. 8 hours) cyclic durability test switching hinge stiffness between low and high states
future_work: Optimizing the finger structure design to shorten the time required for stiffness modulation by enhancing heat dissipation
Applying different stiffness-changeable principles to the soft gripper
independent_variables: SMP thermal state (glassy state below Tg vs. rubbery state above Tg)
Ni-Cr wire electrical current and heating duration (0.3 A)
SMA wire actuation state and current (SMA-1 vs. SMA-2, 0.65 A)
Selective hinge activation (hinge-1, hinge-2, or both)
Fingertip contact interface material (PDMS fingernail vs. Ecoflex finger pad)
Target object mass, compliance, and geometry
limitations_inferred: Passive cooling duration of 240 seconds makes the gripper unsuitable for high-speed dynamic or industrial pick-and-place manipulation tasks without active cooling
Actuated SMA wires must be continuously energized during the 240-second cooling period to maintain shape until SMP solidifies, increasing overall energy consumption
Low glass transition temperature of SMP (55 °C) restricts operation in elevated thermal environments where stiffness modulation would fail
Maximum grasping force (5.8 N) remains modest compared to rigid or fluidic high-pressure grippers, limiting applications to light or delicate objects
Absence of integrated embedded curvature or contact force feedback sensors requires open-loop timing-based control
limitations_stated_by_authors: Long operational transition time required for returning from the low-stiffness state to the high-stiffness state due to slow passive heat dissipation of the heated SMP
Inherent softness and small actuation force generated by soft SMA actuators (approx. 10^-3 to 10^-1 N) when unreinforced

Minor discrepancies between theoretical and experimental bending modulus values (mean errors of 5.6% in high stiffness and 1.7% in low stiffness) caused by SMP fabrication tolerances and positioning errors during embedding
main_results: Fabricated a 3-finger SMA-based soft gripper incorporating 3D-printed SMP variable-stiffness hinges and Ecoflex fingertip pads
Achieved an experimental bending modulus ratio of approximately 55.62 times between glassy state (128.48 MPa) and rubbery state (2.31 MPa) in the hinge structures
Achieved 9 distinct shape-retained postures per finger through selective independent hinge softening and bidirectional SMA actuation
Increased maximum vertical pulling force on a fixed cylinder by approximately 10-fold (from 0.6 N in low-stiffness state to 5.8 N in high-stiffness state)

Demonstrated stable grasping of delicate, deformable, heavy, and complex shapes, including successful picking up of a 3D-printed frustum-shaped object using preparatory posture configuration and finger pad area contact
modeling_methods: Composite beam flexural rigidity formulation summing constituent second moments of area: E_H * I_H = E_PDMS * I_PDMS + E_SMP * I_SMP
Theoretical bending modulus estimation based on modular ratio: E_H = (1 - alpha) * E_PDMS + alpha * E_SMP, where alpha = I_SMP / I_H
Three-point bending calculation using ASTM D 790-03 load-displacement gradient: E_H = (L^3 * m) / (4 * w_1 * (2*t_1 + t_2)^3)
SMA constitutive and beam bending deformation modeling referenced via Brinson constitutive model and Euler beam theory
Quasi-static 2D vertical equilibrium force analysis for frustum grasping comparing point-contact fingernail vs. area-contact finger pad mechanics: G = 2 * F * (mu * sin(theta) - cos(theta))
performance_metrics: SMP heating time to reach glass transition temperature (55 °C): approx. 30 s; heating to 60 °C: approx. 35 s
SMP cooling time to return to glassy state: approx. 240 s
SMA bending actuation time: approx. 5 s
Hinge bending modulus: 128.48 MPa (high stiffness) vs. 2.31 MPa (low stiffness), representing an approx. 55.62-fold ratio and ~98% modulus loss upon heating
Theoretical hinge bending modulus: 136.10 MPa (high stiffness) vs. 2.35 MPa (low stiffness)
Gripper pulling force: 5.8 N (high stiffness) vs. 0.6 N (low stiffness), representing an approx. 10-fold enhancement
Static and dynamic coefficients of friction: PDMS on ABS (4.56 static, 2.92 dynamic) vs. Ecoflex on ABS (2.45 static, 2.18 dynamic)
Calculated grasping weight capacity ratio for frustum object using finger pad vs. fingernail: approx. 1.93 times higher
Cyclic durability: maintained multi-configuration capability over 100 continuous cycles (approx. 8 hours)
possible_gap_implications: Demonstrates that thermally induced phase change can resolve the force-density drawback of soft SMA grippers, but highlights slow thermal dissipation as a critical barrier, motivating research into active cooling or non-thermal variable-stiffness mechanisms

Suggests that multi-joint soft digits capable of multi-posture pre-shaping and area contact provide substantial grasping advantages over monolithic single-curvature soft fingers for complex geometries
paper.research_objective: To develop an SMA-based soft gripper with variable stiffness by integrating shape memory polymer (SMP) structures into composite hinges, enabling compliant shape-morphing in a low-stiffness state, high-stiffness shape retention for lifting heavier loads, and multi-posture adaptation for complex geometries.
paper.research_problem: Inherent softness and small actuation force in soft SMA-based robotic grippers limit their load capacity, while conventional designs require continuous energy input to maintain deformation and cannot reconfigure finger postures for objects of varying and complex shapes.
paper.title: Shape Memory Alloy-Based Soft Gripper with Variable Stiffness for Compliant and Effective Grasping
